**S3 plan for #31520, measured on main `95df3459`. No code yet.**

`cd ui && node scripts/select-affected-tests.mjs --base origin/main --explain` gives 519 always-on files. All the figures below come from an instrumented scratch copy of the selector, run on the live tree and since deleted. That copy records which fail-closed line in `readRadius` refused each file. Where several files in a test's closure are refused, the test is counted under the first reason in this order: library, spawn, cwd, glob, walk, unresolved read, then out-of-owner read.

### 1. The count with `scripts/` and `eslint-rules/` as owner directories

The S3 rule: each of the two directories becomes a pseudo-package with no dependencies, and `scripts/invoked-as.mjs` stops counting as a disk reader.

| variant | always-on |
|---|---:|
| main today | 519 |
| owner directories only | 502 (−17) |
| **owner directories + `invoked-as.mjs` benign (S3 as planned)** | **483 (−36)** |

The 36 files freed are 11 `eslint-rules/` tests, 10 `scripts/__tests__` tests, and 15 package tests whose only out-of-package reads land in `scripts/`. The plan estimated about 80. Most `scripts/` tests read the tree, so they stay always-on.

Why the 483 stay always-on:

| reason | files | of which in `scripts/` or `eslint-rules/` |
|---|---:|---:|
| unresolved read (a variable, a helper parameter, a walk result) | 156 | 32 |
| library reader (`typescript`, `vite`, `tailwindcss`, `postcss`) | 139 | 67 |
| spawn, async `fs` or a glob library (`child_process` in 122 closures) | 79 | 49 |
| `process.cwd()`, `createRequire`, `require.resolve` | 63 | 6 |
| a read outside the ui tree (into the monorepo) | 15 | 0 |
| a walked root | 15 | 4 |
| an `fs` binding used other than as a call | 7 | 2 |
| `import.meta.glob` | 6 | 1 |
| reaches the tree root (`objectstack-skill.test.ts`, `designerRegistrationInputs-11434.test.ts`) | 2 | 0 |
| a read outside every owner | 1 | 1 |
| outside every package | 0 | — |
| undeclared import | 0 | — |

### 2. What selects a `scripts/` test once its directory is an owner

- **A `ui/scripts/` change** makes the `scripts` owner affected. Its directory filter `scripts/` then selects all 172 `scripts/` tests. No tracked test outside `ui/scripts/` has `scripts/` in its path (I checked, 0), so the substring filter does not over-select. `eslint-rules/` works the same way: 11 tests, and no other path contains it.
- **A monorepo-root `scripts/` change arriving as `outside`.** If it is the walker file (`PATH_WALKER_FILE`), the `scripts` owner is affected. The S2 control ("the walker selects what the selector itself does") then stops being trivially true and starts to check something. Any other root file reaches ui tests only through a relative import or a read that leaves the tree. Those tests stay always-on (the 15 and 2 rows above), so nothing narrows.
- **The selector itself** sits in the owner directory, so a change to it selects every `scripts/` test, its own tests included.
- **A package change.** A `scripts/` test that imports a workspace package by name (the owner declares no dependencies) or reads into a package is selected through S1/S2 input packages, as for any package test.
- **A trap found while prototyping.** `configReach` counts a root-config-reached file only when `owningPackage` finds no owner. With the owner directories in the package list, `scripts/vitest-invocation-guard.mjs` would stop being a full-run trigger. S3 must compute `configReach` against the real workspace packages. A control will pin that a change to that file still gives `mode=full`.
- **Full-tree gate tests stay always-on.** They spawn the gate, read `git ls-files` output, walk from the root, or read through a variable, and `readRadius` refuses each of those. Controls will be a fixture `scripts/` test that spawns and one that walks from `process.cwd()`, both kept always-on, plus a fixture test that reads only its own directory, freed. Two more controls: a change to the walker file selects the `scripts/` filter, and a change to `scripts/vitest-invocation-guard.mjs` gives `mode=full`.
- **`invoked-as.mjs` exemption.** It is named in one constant, and a pin reads its `fs` and `child_process` import list. Its disk uses are `realpathSync(process.argv[1])` and a `selfTest` that writes and spawns temp files, so they read no test input. If the import list changes, the pin goes red, so the exemption cannot quietly widen.

**Finding outside S3's frame: a pre-existing blind spot, not an S2 regression.** The library-reader rule applies only inside a file that also imports `fs`. 21 placed tests run a TypeScript, vite or eslint program and touch no `fs`, for example `*.types.test.ts` and `sdui-intrinsics-compile-11075.test.ts`. Such a program reads `tsconfig` and every source it resolves. On this tree, those 21 tests are selected only by their own package, as they were before #31520. Fail-closed would treat a program-level library call as a disk read, which adds up to 21 to the count (483 → ~504). I recommend folding it into S3. It is your call.

### 3. The under-200 route, measured on top of S3 (483)

Each lever was simulated in the scratch copy by rewriting the source before the walker reads it.

| route | projected | files and packages touched | governed path? |
|---|---:|---|---|
